claim: For every \(m,n\ge1\) and \(r\ge0\), let \(A_{m,n}=\mathbf L_m^n\), where \(\mathbf L_m=\{0,1/m,\ldots,1\}\) is the finite Łukasiewicz MV-chain, equipped with coordinatewise MV operations and global constant minimum/maximum quantifiers. An ordered \(r\)-tuple \(g_1,\ldots,g_r\) generates \(A_{m,n}\) exactly when the \(n\) coordinate words \((m g_1(i),\ldots,m g_r(i))\in\{0,\ldots,m\}^r\) are pairwise distinct and \(\gcd(m,\{m g_j(i)\})=1\), with the empty gcd interpreted as \(m\). The number of ordered generating tuples is \(N_{m,n,r}=\sum_{d\mid m}\mu(d)\big((m/d+1)^r\big)_{\underline n}\), where the subscript denotes a falling factorial. The minimum generator rank equals \(\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\) for \(m=1\) and \(\max\{1,\lceil\log_{m+1}n\rceil\}\) for \(m\ge2\). For fixed \(m\ge2\), independently uniform generator entries and \(Q=(m+1)^r\), \(\Pr(\langle\mathbf g\rangle=A_{m,n})\to e^{-\lambda^2/2}\) whenever \(n,r\to\infty\) and \(n/\sqrt Q\to\lambda\in[0,\infty)\), and the probability tends to zero if \(n/\sqrt Q\to\infty\).

correctness.rationale: The necessity invariants hold by induction on all signature operations: equal coordinate words remain equal, and values lying in the multiples-of-d subchain remain there even under global extrema. The functions h_a(x)=max(0,1-m|x-a/m|) are continuous integer-affine pieces and hence standard McNaughton unary term functions; they construct crisp coordinate selectors. Extracting generator entries with global maximum, applying Euclidean truncated subtraction to numerators, and masking constant truth levels reconstructs every vector exactly when the gcd is one. Möbius inversion counts injections with gcd one; a word containing numerator 1 proves the exact rank; an explicit prime-divisor union bound and birthday expansion prove the random threshold. All parameter boundaries including m=n=1 and r=0 were checked. The actual verifier completed 5968 direct tuple closures, 53 independent signature counts and 14 peak-term searches; finite tests support but do not replace the general proof.

title: Arithmetic generator census and birthday threshold for finite monadic MV powers

value.rationale: The specified finite functional monadic MV powers are central finite witnesses in the cited 2024 S5-modal Łukasiewicz completeness framework. Asking for complete expressivity from a prescribed number of propositions is a natural sharp generator problem, not an arbitrarily sliced example. The theorem identifies separate coordinate-separation and primitive-arithmetic obstructions, supplies the closed Möbius census and minimum rank for all parameters, and proves a sharp two-to-one logarithmic separation between extremal and typical random generator thresholds. The many-valued MV arithmetic criterion is substantively different from the prior Gödel zero-pattern/coverage criterion.
